facts.program: Total Home Energy Savings Program (NB Power)
facts.claim: Rebates for homeowners who upgrade doors, insulation, heating or windows after a Home Energy Evaluation by a Certified Energy Advisor. Steps: register online or call 1-800-663-6272; get the evaluation; review the report; finish upgrades within 9 months of the evaluation; a final inspection gives a new EnerGuide rating; rebates are paid from saved receipts, by e-Transfer or direct deposit.
facts.amount: See the space heating, water heating, insulation and additional rebate facts.
facts.eligibility: If you own a home, the program is for you. Energy upgrades can also lower your mortgage insurance premium by up to 25%, per the page.
facts.dates: No closing date stated. Solar and oil advance funding have their own dates (see those facts).
facts.notes: Read on 2026-10-21. The cost to join and exact eligibility rules are in the program guidelines, which were not read.

facts.program: Total Home space heating equipment rebates (NB Power)
facts.claim: Rebates when you upgrade your existing primary heating system.
facts.amount: Central ducted air source heat pump $1,500. Furnace heat pump add-on $1,000. Geothermal heat pump $2,000. Mini split heat pump $400. Multizone heat pump $350 per indoor head. Pellet stove $500. Propane or natural gas fireplace insert $200 (70% efficiency or higher). Wood or pellet boiler or furnace $500. Wood or pellet fireplace insert $200. Wood stove $200.
facts.eligibility: Air source heat pumps must be on NB Power's qualifying list. Furnace add-on: ENERGY STAR or on that list. Geothermal: Canada Greener Homes Grant ground source list or ENERGY STAR. Wood and pellet equipment: US EPA or CSA B415.1 rated and WETT installed. Existing primary heating system requirements are in the program guidelines.
facts.notes: Read on 2026-10-21. Third-party pages that list other amounts (such as a single $2,000 maximum) are out of date or wrong.

facts.program: Total Home water heating equipment rebates (NB Power)
facts.claim: Rebates when you upgrade your existing water heating system.
facts.amount: Heat pump water heater $550 (ENERGY STAR). Drain water heat recovery $400 (heat recovery efficiency 42% or more).
facts.eligibility: See the program guidelines for equipment lists.

facts.claim: Insulation incentives when you insulate at least 20% of a total building component area (for example 20% of the total ceiling area). Legible receipts or invoices are needed at the final evaluation. If you remove mouldy or compressed insulation, you must replace the amount removed plus the minimum to add.
facts.amount: Per square foot by R-value added. Attic (minimum add R-15, maximum after R-60): $0.40 at R-15, $0.45 at R-20, $0.65 at R-40, $0.85 at R-60. Exterior and main walls (minimum add R-7.5, maximum R-30): $1.125 at R-7.5, $1.25 at R-10, $1.75 at R-20, $2.25 at R-30. Basement or crawlspace walls (minimum add R-10, maximum R-30): $1.00 at R-10, $1.50 at R-20, $2.00 at R-30. Basement header (minimum add R-20, maximum R-40): $1.00 at R-20, $2.00 at R-30, $3.00 at R-40. Exposed floor (minimum add R-10, maximum R-30): $1.00 at R-10, $2.00 at R-20, $3.00 at R-30. Basement slab (minimum add R-3.5, maximum R-20): $0.55 at R-3.5, $1.20 at R-10, $2.20 at R-20.
facts.eligibility: Amounts between the listed R-values are also paid. See the program guidelines for details.
facts.notes: Read on 2026-10-21. The page says the tables have been shortened to save space.

facts.program: Total Home windows, ventilation and air sealing rebates (NB Power)
facts.claim: Additional incentives for windows, doors and skylights, heat recovery ventilators and air sealing.
facts.amount: Windows, doors and skylights: $50 each (ENERGY STAR; keep the stickers). Heat recovery ventilator: $200 (ENERGY STAR). Air sealing, sliding scale for actual air leakage reduction: 10% $250, 15% $350, 20% $450, 25% $550.
facts.eligibility: No air sealing incentive if the home was at 3 air changes per hour or less at the initial evaluation, or if the home's volume changes (such as an addition or a flat ceiling changed to cathedral).

facts.claim: Solar photovoltaic incentive of $200 per kW, only for people who enrolled in the Total Home Energy Savings Program by May 27, 2026. Work must be complete and a final Home Energy Evaluation done on or before January 31, 2027. Projects must meet NB Power's net metering program requirements.
facts.eligibility: Enrolled by May 27, 2026 (closed to new enrolments). Net metering requirements.
facts.dates: Enrolment closed May 27, 2026. Final evaluation by January 31, 2027.
facts.notes: Read on 2026-10-21. Closed for anyone not already enrolled.

facts.program: NB oil to heat pump advance funding (Total Home)
facts.claim: Registrations for the advance payment to switch from oil to a heat pump closed June 30, 2026. Registered households must finish the upgrade by March 31, 2027. To get an advance payment, all required paperwork had to be submitted by October 1, 2026. The space heating page says 'Switching off oil? You may be eligible for up to $15,000 to help make the move to heat pumps more affordable.'
facts.amount: Up to $15,000 (headline on the space heating page; conditions not read)
facts.eligibility: Not confirmed. The page that explains who qualifies returned a 404 on 2026-10-21, so income and household rules are unverified.
facts.dates: Registration closed June 30, 2026. Paperwork due October 1, 2026. Upgrade complete by March 31, 2027.
facts.notes: Dates read on the program page and the $15,000 line on the space heating page on 2026-10-21. Do not state the income table or who qualifies.

facts.program: Enhanced Energy Savings Program (NB Power, income-based)
facts.claim: Program open to eligible New Brunswick homeowners however they heat. Registration is online; NB Power screens by household income and need for upgrades. First-come, first-served, subject to program funding; successful applicants are contacted.
facts.amount: Not stated on the eligibility page (it does not say what the upgrades cost the household).
facts.eligibility: Annual combined gross household income under $70,000 (line 15000 of the latest Notice of Assessment for each adult 19 or older). You own and live in the home. The home needs energy efficiency upgrades. A home with electric baseboards and no mini-split may get a mini-split recommended. A home heated only by an oil furnace or boiler may get a cold climate air source heat pump or another system recommended. Already in Total Home? Email SmartHabits@nbpower.com.
facts.notes: Read on 2026-10-21. Search summaries call these 'free upgrades'; the eligibility page does not, so no page says free.
